cefrAlignment: Matches B1: everyday notices and emails, a timetable, a 280-word article on a familiar topic and core grammar. This covers the B1 can-do descriptors for reading correspondence, reading for orientation and reading for information in one 45-minute test.
examFidelity: The 41 items cover TOEIC Part 5 and Part 7, IELTS headings, True/False/Not Given and short answers, and TOEFL Complete the Words. I checked the timetable answers against the table (Tuesday; £10 less 20% = £8). Each False contradicts the text and each Not Given is truly absent. Q23 'it' = walking to school is verified: it is the only defensible option, because 'it wasn't safe' repeats 'walking wasn't safe'. The section timings add up to 45 minutes.
fixes: Q27 was almost identical to an item in the word-forms lesson ('since 2019 / has worked'). I replaced it with a past simple item using 'ago', so the review tests a different time word
Complete the Words paragraph was 56 words, below the 70–100 in exams.ts. I added one complete closing sentence (now about 78 words); the damaged words did not change
Q38: added 'nings' and 'evenings' as accepted answers
Q23 explanation: added a substitution test ('the cars were the reason walking to school wasn't safe')
Moved the correct option in Q2, Q22, Q25, Q26, Q29 and Q30, because most keys were in position B
openConcerns: The score bands (36–41 'ready for B2', etc.) are the writer's own estimates and have not been calibrated. The tip says this, but a specialist could check them against real learner data.
learnerOutcome: A learner can measure their B1 reading across the main exam formats in 45 minutes and see which course lesson to review, based on the section where they lost marks.
